Team —

Attached: Q3-OKR-status-sheet.xlsx (tabbed by initiative) + canary-rollout-plan.pdf (prod gating checklist). High level status for the midrun checkpoint and proposed re-scopes below — ask in bold at the end.

1) Product / Serving throughput (OKR: 2x p99 throughput for small models) — At risk (amber).
   - What’s green: kernel selection optimization landed, perf regressed fixed in 10/2 build.
   - What’s amber: autoscaler instability under mixed batch workloads; observed 15% throttle during peak.
   - Proposed re-scope: push non-critical throughput targets from Oct sprint to Nov, preserve latency SLO work.

2) Dedicated onboarding (OKR: 20 customers onboarded) — On track with caveats.
   - Blocker: procurement contract turnaround for Daejin & Atlas Labs (legal + procurement).
   - Proposed re-scope: prioritize Atlas Labs pilot (highest strategic value), move 4 lower-touch customers to next wave.

3) Quality/Regression monitoring (OKR: establish eval baseline & alerts) — Behind.
   - Need: 2-week eval harness run & labeled prompt set; engineering needs more test JVM capacity to run golden sets concurrently.

Asks (what I need from each of you):
- @Markus: can infra dedicate a short-term test pool (4 gpus) for the eval harness for Oct 12–26? If not, what alternative?
- @Vanessa: can CS provide priority customer-impact examples (3 bullets per customer) for Atlas + Daejin by EOD Oct 12 so we can shape the QBR deck?
- @Naomi: we need a one-page QBR artifact capturing customer impact and remediation plan by Oct 15; can you lead consolidation?

If we don’t land the infra bump and procurement exceptions by Oct 20, we will lose pilot momentum and should escalate. I’ve highlighted conservative re-scope suggestions in the attached workbook.

Thanks — short replies preferred so I can roll into leadership readout Tuesday.

—Rachel
Rachel Kim | Director, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
